pr_title: keys: fix addressing of RKeyMin derivates
pr_body:
This patch fixes a problem with RangeMetaKey(RKeyMin.Next()). This was
returning a Meta2 key, when it should have returned a Meta1 key (like
RangeMetaKey(RKeyMin) does).
This was having spectacular consequences for the range cache: evicting
the Meta1 descriptor from the cache was always failing because the
eviction is trying to find the descriptor by startKey.Next() (so
RKeyMin.Next()), and that retrieval was failing to find the descriptor
since it was skipping over the right cache entry (the cache entry is
keyed by RangeMetaKey(endKey), so it was a Meta1 key). This was causing
requests that were encoutering a NLHE on the Meta1 range to spin forever
since it was looking to the DistSender like the lease received in the
error was perpetualy stale (since it was failing to evict anything from
the cache).

Fixes #52468
Fixes #52391

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/52786)
Good catch, but spend a few more words so Nathan and I can fully appreciate when we hit this.

I'm closing this in favor of a different fix in #52817.
I've got cold feet after running into some trouble; our key space has some quirks. I've opened #52820 that adds a note hinting to the issues.

issue_context.title: backupccl: RESTORE got stuck shortly after starting
issue_context.body:
I'm filing this issue mainly to track this in case it shows up in any further testing.

When restoring the `restore2TB` backup to a 24 node cluster, it quickly imported 50 GiB, and then the live bytes on the cluster stopped increasing as did the storage traffic (after about 2 minutes - which might be around the time that all the ranges finished scattering). Unfortunately, the cluster was wiped before I was able to grab the logs from the cluster.
